title: five of pentacles: on self-exile and inner refuge
content:
this is tarot work guides — in which I draw one card a week to explore as a guide for my creative business practice.

guiding question for 5 of Pentacles:

in which ways am I exiling and alienating myself with scarcity narratives — when a sacred refuge is right in front of me? what does that refuge look and feel like?

—

on the friday of the week I drew the 5 of Pentacles, my partner K and I found ourselves in a very literal experience of this card — slogging ourselves around the city on a blistering snowy day, umbrella-less, our socks drenched and wet, as we collected bureaucratic paperwork for my Turkish residency permit. while standing in a long line outside the immigration office, my partner pointed out that next to us was an old Greek Orthodox church from the Ottoman era. here was a historical place of refuge, next to a crowd of foreigners seeking refuge, of some kind or other. I drew about this experience in this visual diary.

in my case, our physical journey of wandering in the cold ended when we got home. I put on fuzzy socks, made a cup of tea, and wrapped myself in thick blankets on the couch.

now, I’ll unpack the metaphorical journey of the 5 of Pentacles — and how I’ve transformed it from a card I used to dread pulling — to one that asks me to dig through my scarcity narratives, and transform them into something new.

exploring scarcity narratives

in the days leading up to that literal snowy excursion, I spent the week meditating on the themes in this card — of scarcity, alienation, and limitation.

here’s some questions I journaled around:

  1. in what ways am I feeling scarcity or a sense of not-enoughness in my life? — in relationship to money, time, resources, or in failing to meet my own expectations?

  2. how am I alienating myself? where am I blaming, shaming, judging, or criticizing myself, or others? where am I the victim?

  3. where do I feel my limitations? which limitations are supporting me? which ones feel depleting?


the 5 of Pentacles is a archetype of material poverty and hardship. I interpret this to mean that scarcity narratives are like metaphorical excursions in the cold — but ending with a thick blanket and a cup of tea on the couch, these narratives often silently lurk, for years, in the backcloset of the mind.

when I draw this card, I can often relate it to something that happens (an unexpected bill, a rejection, an email) that triggers that scarcity. suddenly, I’ve thrown myself into the winter blizzard, oblivious to any and all possible resources available to me. I feel poor, crippled, and blind; cut off from my own sense of creative possibility and inner power, and only aware of how I don’t have enough — time, money, skills, or energy. the 5 of Pentacles captures a moment in which I feel that I don’t have enough. that I am not enough.

the many forms of self exile

it took me some time to articulate these feelings — at its root — as forms of self-exile. in a deeply spiritual sense, self-exile is a poverty consciousness and alienation from oneself; a disintegration of the self is the opposite of feeling whole and resourced. if you’re moving through the world with exiled parts, then it only makes sense that those exiled parts will cause heaviness, resistance, and friction.

for me, my self-exile is often triggered by feelings of perfectionism, a desire to control the uncontrollable, or feeling overly responsible and self-blaming for things I can’t control. my personal context is that I drew this card while working on a year-long web development project like a leviathan that severely triggered the anxious perfectionist in me — and, it was showing up as I was beginning to write about a cafe investment betrayal I experienced last fall, which still had its reverberating effects in my financial sense of safety.

in some ways, drawing this card can feel like a relief.

I saw it as an invitation to search within myself — with the gentle magnifying glass of my attention — to see, exactly, where in my life I’m telling myself that I’m poor and powerless, not-enough, un-resourced, and alone. I ask myself if I truly believe that’s true — or a narrative loop I’m living through.

then, I look for the refuge and abundance I’m walking past, and missing.

accessing inner refuge

the 5 of Pentacles makes me think about the number 5 in the Major Arcana — The Hierophant — as an archetype of the spiritual leader standing behind those stained glass windows, speaking on a podium to a gathered community.

whereas 5 of Pentacles represents self-alienation and isolation, the Hierophant represents integration — a spiritual leader empowered enough to serve as a bridge; a sacred channel between the spiritual and the earthly worlds. in this sense, you could see these two cards as mirrors to each other, both connected by the number 5.

when I’m feeling trapped in narratives of scarcity and not-enoughness, the most important thing I can remind myself is the nature of non-duality.

I am both inside AND outside that church.

I am both the figures wandering outside in the blizzard, and, I am the abundance that resides inside the warm refuge of the church. I don’t take the word “church” literally, but as a metaphorical space of sacred belonging and sufficiency — where I can trust that all of my spiritual and material needs will be met. and more.

from scarcity to sacredness

so, how do we get there?

how do we move from the metaphorical coldness of alienation and scarcity — to a sacred refuge of belonging?

as with all inner journeys, I think it begins with identifying the concrete, small ways in which we self-exile, and deliberately choosing to replace those thought patterns with self-trust and healing — even if it feels hard and strange, at first.

this might look like the tedious work of shining a flashlight on lurking thoughts, and bringing them to the light.

here’s two examples.

boundaries & limitations

it might mean identifying what parts of your work — or ways of working — makes you feel nourished and integrated, rather than depleted and striving, cornering you into battling feelings of not-enoughness and perfectionism. perhaps this journey requires that you create boundaries to respect your own energy limitations — to not feel pressure to give more at all costs, but to give fully from what’s available. maybe it’s about cherishing your own sacred energy — by creating a container where you can feel safe. maybe, this means nurturing a creative business like a hammock, designed to allow you to rest.

control & surrender

or, maybe it means holdly tenderly and facing your need to control outcomes — that which feels like thrusting yourself into the cold blizzard of your own high standards, again and again. maybe this means beginning by sensing, with your body, what it feels like to release the urge to control. what if you trusted? what if you surrendered? could you even imagine??

what if you don’t have to walk for miles in the cold — just to prove that you are worthy, and enough, and deserving of good things?

what if that refuge — of enoughness, of belonging, of abundance — is a sacred place within you? what would that place feel like? how can you guide yourself to visit it, in small moments, everyday?
